47	- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
48	- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
49	- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.
50	
51	Surface habits:
52	
53	- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
54	- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
55	- A bar down one side of a rounded box (a one-sided border, inset shadow or pseudo-element), any colour or state. Use a full border, a tint, or a leading icon or label.
56	- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
57	- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
58	- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
59	- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering (Google: `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable font-fetch <Family>`); the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
60	- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
61	- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
62	- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.
63	
64	The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.
65	# Operate
66	
67	`impeccable concept-seed --mode operate` prints the two sections below as its MODE RULES block. On an Operate surface the visitor came to get a job done, so the page is first a working product of its category and the world serves it.
68	
69	## Directions
70	
71	Someone who uses tools like this one should know where everything is before they notice the world. The world lends four things and only these: type, palette, density, and one signature move. It never supplies the layout, the navigation model, or the controls. Colour is part of the world's contribution, and it does real jobs: a committed palette for the shell (a coloured rail or header, a tinted ground), state colours, data series, selection, and the signature move. A grey screen with one accent colour is the category default without the category's polish, not restraint.
72	
73	Read every candidate, the assigned direction, and every challenger through that limit before you fuse or judge it. A world taken from a tool or instrument the audience operates (a terminal, a scope, a control panel, a cockpit) or from a fictional interface comes back as a costume of that tool on a working screen: take from it only what transfers as type, palette, density, and a signature move, or replace it from your list. When a catalog world's source is itself an interface language, the same limit holds: it lends type, density, palette, and one signature move, while navigation and controls stay the standard ones for the platform, web components on the web and native controls in an app.
74	
75	Write each direction's first viewport as the product's shell first: the navigation, the work areas and what each is for, the data the visitor reads first and its states, and then where the signature move lives. Expression may never obscure the task, state, or familiar affordance. Name the signature move concretely, so the comp and the build can find it: service health drawn as a transit map, a schedule set in a timetable's column rhythm. A direction whose world shows up only as a colour scheme has not found its move yet. When you weigh fused challengers, product clarity includes reading as a working product of this category.
76	
77	## Comps
78	
79	The comp is the product screen, in the direction's committed palette: its shell and navigation with a distinct area for each job and, where there is data, filters over what they scope and charts and tables with clear states. The world enters only through type, palette, density, and the one signature move; it never supplies the page's organisation, so a working screen never reads as a newspaper, a poster, or any other artifact of the world. Every control is a standard one the visitor already knows how to use, a web component on the web and the platform's native control in an app: buttons, tabs, inputs, selects, filters, tables with sortable headers, navigation that reads as navigation. Never a costume of the world's own interface: a terminal's function-key bar or command prompt, an instrument's bezel, ruled ledger paper standing in for a table. A comp an engineer could not build from the platform's standard components is a picture of the tool, not the tool. The finish bar is the best product in the category: an aligned grid, consistent spacing, a real type scale, and clear hierarchy. The signature move adds to a screen that is already that clean; it never stands in for it.
80	
81	Prompt with the screen's real content: the product name, realistic data with plausible values and units, real labels, and one state worth seeing (an alert, a degraded service, an empty filter result), never placeholder tiles. State colours (red for critical, amber for degraded) sit on top of the world's palette only where they carry meaning, and a headline number that moves over time shows its recent history, with the onset marked when something changed.
82	
83	Comps two and three vary the product's organisation, never its world coverage: the navigation model (side rail, top bar, command-first), how the work areas divide the screen, which data leads, the density, and where the signature move sits. Each must be recognisably different from the first at thumbnail size; a variant only its prompt can tell apart adds no choice. A variant that adds world material, texture, or ornament goes further in the wrong direction; on a working screen, more world is a costume.
84	
85	Self-check every render: with the name covered, does it read as a product of its category, could the visitor do the task from it, and is it at least as clean as the category standard and more distinctive than it? If it reads as an artifact of the world first, regenerate with the shell and the work areas named region by region and the world held to its four contributions.
86	# Operate mode depth (and Read notes)
87	
88	When design SERVES the product: app UIs, admin dashboards, settings panels, data tables, tools, authenticated surfaces, anything where the user is in a task. The essentials live in SKILL.md's modes and [craft-floor.md](craft-floor.md); this file is extended depth, written for Operate surfaces. Read surfaces (docs, guides, long-form) take SKILL.md's Read mode plus this file's typography and consistency rules; their prose measure and navigation matter more than component density.
89	
90	## The product slop test
91	
92	Familiarity is often a feature here. The test is whether a category-fluent user can trust the interface immediately or must pause at every subtly-off component.
93	
94	Product UI's failure mode isn't flatness, it's strangeness without purpose: over-decorated buttons, mismatched form controls, gratuitous motion, display fonts where labels should be, invented affordances for standard tasks. The bar is earned familiarity. The tool should disappear into the task.
95	
96	## Typography
97	
98	- **One family is often right.** Product UIs don't need display/body pairing. A well-tuned sans carries headings, buttons, labels, body, data.
99	- **Fixed rem scale, not fluid.** Clamp-sized headings don't serve product UI. Users view at consistent DPI, and a fluid h1 that shrinks in a sidebar looks worse, not better.
100	- **Tighter scale ratio.** 1.125–1.2 between steps is typical. More type elements here than on brand surfaces; exaggerated contrast creates noise.
101	- **Line length still applies for prose** (65–75ch). Data and compact UI can run denser; tables at 120ch+ are fine.
102	
103	## Color
104	
105	Product defaults to Restrained. A single surface can earn Committed (a dashboard where one category color carries a report, an onboarding flow with a drenched welcome screen), but Restrained is the floor.
106	
107	- State-rich semantic vocabulary: hover, focus, active, disabled, selected, loading, error, warning, success, info. Standardize these.
108	- Accent color used for primary actions, current selection, and state indicators only, not decoration.
109	- A second neutral layer for sidebars, toolbars, and panels (slightly cooler or warmer than the content surface).
110	
111	## Layout
112	
113	- Responsive behavior is structural (collapse sidebar, responsive table, breakpoint-driven columns), not fluid typography.
114	
115	## Components
116	
117	Every interactive component has: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error. Don't ship with half of these.
118	
119	- Skeleton states for loading, not spinners in the middle of content.
120	- Empty states that teach the interface, not "nothing here."
121	- Consistent affordances across the surface. Same button shape. Same form-control vocabulary. Same icon style.
122	- Overlays escape their container. An absolutely positioned dropdown inside an `overflow: hidden` or `overflow: auto` ancestor gets clipped; reach for `<dialog>`, the popover API, `position: fixed`, or a portal.
123	
124	## Motion
125	
126	- 150–250 ms on most transitions. Users are in flow; don't make them wait for choreography.
127	- Motion conveys state, not decoration. State change, feedback, loading, reveal: nothing else.
128	- No orchestrated page-load sequences. Product loads into a task; users don't want to watch it load.
129	
130	## Product constraints
131	
132	- Decorative motion that doesn't convey state.
133	- Inconsistent component vocabulary across screens. If the "save" button looks different in two places, one is wrong.
134	- Display fonts in UI labels, buttons, data.
135	- Reinventing standard affordances for flavor (custom scrollbars, weird form controls, non-standard modals).
136	- Heavy color or full-saturation accents on inactive states.
137	- Modal as first thought. Modals are usually laziness. Exhaust inline / progressive alternatives first.
138	
139	## Product permissions
140	
141	Product can afford things brand surfaces can't.
142	
143	- System fonts and familiar sans defaults.
144	- Standard navigation patterns: top bar + side nav, breadcrumbs, tabs, command palettes.
145	- Density. Tables with many rows, panels with many labels, dense information when users need it.
146	- Consistency over surprise. The same visual vocabulary screen to screen is a virtue; delight is saved for moments, not pages.
147	# New visual work
148	
149	Use this flow for a new surface or a replacement visual identity. PRODUCT.md owns product truth. DESIGN.md owns durable visual decisions. A surface brief keeps strategy that belongs to one route or artifact. Complete [init.md](init.md) first when PRODUCT.md is missing; a missing DESIGN.md does not route back to init.
150	
151	For a chosen comp’s region map, see [region-map.md](region-map.md) for the command sequence and schema.
152	
153	## 1. Decide what is already true
154	
155	Read DESIGN.md, representative code, tokens, components, and assets.
156	
157	- **Redesign:** preserve product truth, content, function, constraints, and explicit brand commitments; replace the old visual world rather than polishing it. The old look is evidence of what the subject is, not authority over what it becomes.
158	- **Established world:** inherit it. A missing DESIGN.md does not erase a coherent identity already in code; document that identity instead of inventing a replacement.
159	- **Incomplete brand:** preserve confirmed assets and recognizable traits, then expand the system with the user for this surface.
160	- **Seeded world:** DESIGN.md's frontmatter names a catalog `world:` (written by `impeccable world <id>`) and no code carries it yet; styles that predate the seed, such as a starter template's CSS, do not carry it. The person already chose this world, so it is the established world even when the boot reports no visual authority: never roll, re-pick, or invent a replacement on your own initiative, but an explicit request from the person for a redesign or a different world overrides this and is a redesign (step 4 of **Create or replace the visual world**, in [new-work-world.md](new-work-world.md
161	- **No visual authority:** create a new world with the user.
162	
163	A section, component, feature, or state inside an established surface inherits that surface. Never turn a local addition into a new identity exercise.
164	
165	## 2. Ask what will change the work
166	
167	Before implementation, get the user's answer through the structured question tool when available. Ask two or three related questions; a precise request needs only a compact confirmation. Skip settled facts, not the confirmation: DESIGN.md settles the visual world, not this surface's purpose or concept.
168	
169	- **Persuade:** who must act, what they should believe, which real proof, content, or assets earn that belief.
170	- **Operate:** the task, information, important states, frequency, constraints.
171	- **Read:** the reader's question, source material, structure, wayfinding.
172	- **Experience:** what leads, how exploration unfolds, which interaction or transition matters.
173	
174	Across modes, ask what success looks like, what must remain untouched, and what would make a polished result feel wrong. Never ask for CSS values or canned aesthetic lanes. On a new or replacement world these are product questions only: propose no look of your own before concept-seed has run, because a direction named in a question is the one the answer confirms.
175	
176	## 3. Choose the right amount of invention
177	
178	### Extend an existing surface
179	
180	Inherit its world and composition. Resolve only the new purpose, content, hierarchy, states, interaction, and how the addition joins the surrounding experience. No concept tournament, and no DESIGN.md change unless the user approves a durable system change.
181	
182	### Create a whole surface inside an established world
183	
184	Keep the visual system fixed. Derive five to seven materially different structures from the content, task, and user behavior, ordered by resonance. For a genuinely open whole page, screen, or flow, run:
185	
186	`.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable concept-seed --scope surface --mode <mode>`
187	
188	The script deals three of your structures; the dice pick which three reach the user, breaking the ranking rut while the user keeps a real choice. Present them on the decision page as full cards of equal salience, the dealt lead under kicker THE ROLL, with steer and re-roll; the user locks one. Each card declares `kind`: `assigned` on the dealt lead, `dealt` on the other dealt structures, and `challenger` with its `catalogId` (the SOURCE ID) on a challenger that won its place. No canon card and no pick card at surface scope: the world is settled, so every card visualizes composition, not identi
189	
190	### Create or replace the visual world
191	
192	Read [new-work-world.md](new-work-world.md) now and follow it: this path's steps, the roll and the decision page live there. Come back for step 4 once a direction is locked.
193	
194	### The build path of a decision round
195	
196	The execution contract, comp-led or code-led, is never asked inside a round; the page's toggle handles the exception. An Operate or Read surface is code-led whatever the project records: working screens and documents come out better built than pictured. A Persuade or Experience surface takes the recorded default: read it from `.impeccable/config.json` (`buildPath`), the gitignored `.impeccable/config.local.json` winning where one machine differs from the team's committed value; with neither, comp-led is the default whenever image generation exists. concept-seed's PRESENTATION block prints the 
197	
198	## 4. Commit the world
199	
200	Pick a color strategy before picking colors: Restrained (neutrals tinted from the world plus one accent; common on screens people operate or read, where the mode's rules still ask colour to do real jobs), Committed (one saturated color carries 30-60% of the surface), Full palette (3-4 named roles), or Drenched (the surface IS the color). Persuade and Experience surfaces have permission for the bolder strategies; take them when the brief allows. Color commits at page scale: fields that own whole regions, not accents scattered over a neutral ground. Dark or light is never a default: write one se
201	
202	Choose faces like objects from the subject's world, in the mode's register. Operate and Read surfaces are well served by system stacks and workhorse UI faces; Persuade and Experience surfaces want faces with a point of view, and these training-data defaults mean you stopped looking: Fraunces, Playfair Display, Cormorant, Lora, Crimson, Newsreader, Syne, Space Grotesk, Space Mono, IBM Plex, Inter-as-display, DM Sans, DM Serif, Outfit, Plus Jakarta Sans, Instrument Sans. Naming one of these faces anyway requires a reason no other face could satisfy, and a subject association is never that reason
203	
204	Calibration: AI-generated interfaces cluster around a few looks regardless of subject: warm cream ground, high-contrast serif display, and a terracotta or signal-red accent; near-black with one neon accent and glowing edges; broadsheet-editorial hairlines, italic display serif, and small tracked mono labels; flat saturated ink with black boxes, hard offset shadows, and heavy condensed display type. All are legitimate when the brief calls for them. Where the brief leaves the aesthetic free, landing in one means the self-check failed: if someone could guess your aesthetic from the category alone
205	
206	Your measured rendition prior: warm, bookish, family, and child-facing subjects come out as cream grounds, serif display with italic accents, and lamplight, even when the assigned direction never asked for them. Treat that first palette as already spent. Before writing code, reread your OWN-WORLD block: when it says cream, paper, parchment, ivory, or lamplight for a Persuade surface the brief did not pin, the rendition failed and you rework it from the world's saturated materials first. The same subject renders as bookcloth, thread, jacket, and endpaper color on other models; nothing about the
207	
208	## 5. Record the decision
209	
210	Before code, record the chosen direction as a development-only contract under `## Direction contract` in the relevant surface brief. A direction contract is durable route or artifact strategy, so create or update the brief even when no other surface strategy needs persistence. Use six short blocks, roughly 150 words; do not spend tool calls counting words. THESIS: the one idea this surface owns and the category-default arrangement it refuses. OWN-WORLD: the palette and component language, specific enough to be recognizable with all content removed. STORY: what the visitor understands, believes
211	
212	Never copy the direction contract into implementation source or any browser-delivered artifact. This includes HTML or framework comments, hidden DOM, `<template>` elements, `data-*` attributes, rendered JSX or TSX output, serialized props or state, React Server Component payloads, client bundles, metadata or JSON-LD, accessibility-only text, and files served beside the artifact. A compiler or optimizer removing development metadata is not a safety boundary. Reviewers and documenters receive the contract from the surface brief.
213	
214	On a new or replacement world, DESIGN.md is written at finish, from the built world, by the shipped documenter (section 7); a rulebook written before the build gets defended against reality instead of describing it, and hands the design-system detector an unstable target. A new world shipped with no DESIGN.md is still an incomplete run. An ordinary extension does not rewrite DESIGN.md.
215	
216	Read the existing surface brief before updating it:
217	
218	`.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable surface-brief read <primary-target>`
219	
220	`.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable surface-brief write <primary-target> <body-file> [related-target ...]`
221	
222	After writing, read the brief once more and verify that all six contract blocks and the seed reference (or `seed: none (unavailable)` when the roll printed that, or `seed: none (pinned)` when a direction pinned whole skipped it) are present before building.
223	
224	Keep the brief small: scope and visitor mode; audience, job, action/task, proof/content, and constraints; chosen direction and memorable moment; unresolved decisions. Do not copy global product truth or DESIGN.md tokens into it.
225	
226	On a comp-led build, whenever any image generation is available (a harness-native tool or the API fallback `impeccable context` reports), the locked direction is visualized before it is built, never skipped: load [visualize.md](visualize.md) and follow it, three compositional options put before the user for approval, the chosen card's decision comp plus two variations. This step is proven to produce the most compositional and ambitious work. A comp locked in a surface-scope structure round has already discharged this round (Create a whole surface inside an established world, above). On a code-
227	
228	For `shape`, return the selected direction to [shape.md](shape.md) and stop before persistence or implementation.
229	
230	## 6. Build with full commitment
231	
232	Build the assigned direction, not a safer interpretation of it. The form supplies structure, reading order, component conventions, and native motion; the product supplies every fact. Commit every atom: nav, buttons, inputs, and links are rebuilt in the form's vocabulary, and a stock component inside a committed form is a lapse. Land the first build fully committed; the passes that follow exist to make the committed thing clear and effective, never to dilute it. In unattended work, the safe rendition is the known risk.
233	
234	### Comp-led: the comp is a measured contract
235	
236	On a comp-led build, read [new-work-comp.md](new-work-comp.md) before writing the spec or any code, and follow it: the measured contract, the spec, and the build-phase gates live there.
237	
238	### Both paths
239	
240	- **The first viewport is a thesis, not a header.** Demonstrate the mechanism immediately, at the scale the form has in life; do not trap the concept inside a standard hero or card shell. The memory test: if someone left after one viewport, what would they describe an hour later? If the honest answer is a mood, the concept has not committed yet.
241	- **Prove, don't claim.** Show the subject doing its job: the interface at work, the mechanism dramatized, specifics a competitor could not copy-paste. Demonstration data is design material: author it at full fidelity and label it synthetic; claims stay uninventable.
242	- **Author the assets; never substitute chrome.** Great surfaces live on carefully made content: names, entries, copy, covers, thumbnails, textures. In greenfield work every blank the ask round left open is yours to author at production fidelity; content is authorable, claims are labelable, no section is omittable. Gradients, glass, generic icon tiles, and many-vertex `clip-path` polygons where an authored asset belongs are the gap wearing chrome; the detector flags the last two.
243	- **Draw a print material in its own technique.** On a code-led build, a world whose illustration is engraved, etched, or pen-and-ink is drawn as line: strokes carry the form, hatching (SVG patterns clipped to each shape) carries the tone, and colour sits inside the lines as a translucent wash. Flat fills under a thin outline read as clip-art, which the finish reviewer sends back for a rebuild. Use the world's own assets or one drawn subject per plate; never write a drawing engine.
244	- **Build the form's web leverage.** When the chosen world names a technique (canvas, WebGL, view transitions, generative motion), build the technique itself, not a static imitation of it.
245	- **Pace the scroll like a studio.** Vary density, scale, image, motion, and quiet inside one grammar; a dense passage earns a quiet one, and the page ends anchored by a real close. One spacing rhythm throughout, with more space above a heading than below it.
246	- **Use real, verified imagery when the brief implies it.** Search for the subject's physical object rather than the category; one decisive photo beats five mediocre ones. Verify stock URLs resolve.
247	- **Author motion as material.** Give the page the form's native motion once, orchestrated, rather than scattered hover effects. Bound expensive effects and keep content visible by default.
248	
249	Preserve semantics, accessibility, performance, responsiveness, project conventions, and working behavior.
250	
251	## 7. Inspect and finish
252	
253	Inspect the surface's target sizes in one capture pass per breakpoint. On the web, `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable first-viewport <page> --thesis <FIRST VIEWPORT's selector> --action <primary action's selector> --capture .impeccable/review` is that pass: it writes `desktop.png` and `mobile.png` and checks the fold, gaps, sample labels (`--figures-supplied` for figures the user gave) and a dead action; build no screenshot harness of your own. On a native platform (`ios` / `android` / `adaptive`), the shipped device classes per OS, captured from the simulator or emulator the way th
254	
255	A capture is evidence only when it is valid, and you validate before you send. Settle or disable entrance motion first: an element hidden by animation timing reads as a missing element and gets fixed into a regression. Capture full-page shots from the document top. Capture the comp comparison at the comp's own pixel dimensions. Then open every file once and confirm it shows what its name claims: no black or blank regions, no wrong section behind a right filename, no half-loaded state. A malformed capture sent onward costs the whole round; the reviewer answers it with `disposition: recapture` a
256	
257	After that confirmation the build thread's polishing is over: no further defect hunts, micro-edit scripts, or rebuilds here (an open build-phase gate is not a defect hunt; it closes as above); whatever remains ships through the handoffs, where a fresh context does the finding better and cheaper. On the web, where this harness runs no design hook, run `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --json` on the changed targets once here, fix what is mechanical, and pass the remaining findings to the reviewer; a hookless web build that skips this ships every tell the hook exists to catch.
258	
259	Then spawn the shipped finish reviewer, `impeccable-finish-reviewer` (`impeccable_finish_reviewer` in codex; `/impeccable-finish-reviewer` in Cursor; on GitHub Copilot say "Use the impeccable-finish-reviewer agent"), with the original request, confirmed answers, the artifact path, the screenshot paths, the direction contract, existing hook findings, the QUALITY BAR card and approved comp paths (a code-led build has no approved comp; the chosen decision comp rides in that slot as the critique reference, named as such), on a comp-led build the build state (`.impeccable/build/state.json`), the sp
260	
261	Act on the disposition word; there are exactly four. **recapture**: the evidence failed, not the build. Recapture what the return names under the capture-validity rules, then run a full review over the new evidence. A review conducted on invalid evidence binds nothing, and a verdict pass may never follow it. **rebuild**: fidelity failed wholesale, not in patches. Skip the fix batch and execute the rebuild immediately: re-derive the named regions, produce the named assets, and send the result back for a fresh full review, never a verdict pass; a rebuild replaces regions wholesale, so the whole 
262	
263	A rebuild and a fix round share one asset rule: a raster either round creates or replaces is still asset work under [visualize.md](visualize.md)'s Produce section and keeps its **provenance** like every build raster, and a raster the round abandons is deleted in the same batch. Before either round's result goes back for review or verdict, run `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable embed-prompt --scan <asset-dir...>` over the directories the artifact's rasters ship from and clear every file it reports by embedding what it is missing: the exact generation prompt for a produced raster, the
264	
265	Report the final verdict under the reviewer's own disposition word and at its actual scope. A verdict pass scores the listed fixes and nothing else: "the reviewer scored all three fixes resolved" is a claim it supports, "no material issues remain" is not. A table with open material findings is never announced as a pass, never softened, and never dressed as whole-surface approval when only a fix list was scored. When the user answers a ship with evidence against it, their own screenshot, a named mismatch with the comp, that evidence outranks every capture you made: put their material in the pac
266	
267	After the last correction, on a new or replacement world or an approved system change where a DESIGN.md already exists at the write boundary, collect the choice [document.md](document.md) requires: show the user the existing file. Ask with the AskUserQuestion tool and wait for the answer before continuing. Offer refresh, overwrite, or merge. A seeded world's first build asks nothing: a seed exists to be replaced by the system the build resolved, so the choice is refresh, keeping the frontmatter's `world:` line and the `seededFrom` key in the sidecar. Then spawn the shipped documenter, `impecca
268	
269	On a comp-led build, record the final review disposition with `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable build-phase finish --disposition <ship|fix|rebuild|recapture>` before the final response. A refused `ship` is an unfinished build; report the outstanding phase with the verdict. Any edit after the last captured gate, a fix for a hook finding after `ship` included, voids that capture: run `finish --disposition ship` again before you stop, which rechecks the current files against the gate and names any recapture it needs. Never record `fix` to end a run over an open gate: take the route th
270	
271	The final response opens with the result, not the process: when the build finished, one line saying the page is ready and exactly how to open it (the running dev server's URL, else the command that serves it, else the file path), then the verdict at its scope; when it did not, that line says what is left and still how to open what exists. Report only findings on files that ship; comps, mocks and snapshots under `.impeccable/` are working material and never carry findings.

# New visual work: create or replace the visual world

The branch of [new-work.md](new-work.md) step 3 for a new or replacement world. Steps 4 to 7 of new-work.md follow it.

### Create or replace the visual world

1. Name the product's unique mechanism in one sentence, the audience's real scene, its cultural home, and what this first surface must prove. Note the page this category always ships and its predictable opposite; both are the rut, kept out of the seven-candidate list. A brief that paints its own picture, a product name, a titled artifact, a governing metaphor, adds its literal reading to the rut: spend at most one candidate on it and derive the rest from elsewhere in the audience's world.
2. From that cultural world, list seven concrete visual systems, artifacts, places, or rituals the audience knows by heart, each with one line on why it resonates and can carry the mechanism and one on how it looks (its ground and main colours, its type voices, the one signature that makes it recognisable), ordered by resonance. # Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here except a line marked as a ban; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render (on the web, one `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable shot <page or url>`), not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A bar down one side of a rounded box (a one-sided border, inset shadow or pseudo-element), any colour or state. Use a full border, a tint, or a leading icon or label.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering (Google: `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable font-fetch <Family>`); the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.
# Operate

`impeccable concept-seed --mode operate` prints the two sections below as its MODE RULES block. On an Operate surface the visitor came to get a job done, so the page is first a working product of its category and the world serves it.

## Directions

Someone who uses tools like this one should know where everything is before they notice the world. The world lends four things and only these: type, palette, density, and one signature move. It never supplies the layout, the navigation model, or the controls. Colour is part of the world's contribution, and it does real jobs: a committed palette for the shell (a coloured rail or header, a tinted ground), state colours, data series, selection, and the signature move. A grey screen with one accent colour is the category default without the category's polish, not restraint.

Read every candidate, the assigned direction, and every challenger through that limit before you fuse or judge it. A world taken from a tool or instrument the audience operates (a terminal, a scope, a control panel, a cockpit) or from a fictional interface comes back as a costume of that tool on a working screen: take from it only what transfers as type, palette, density, and a signature move, or replace it from your list. When a catalog world's source is itself an interface language, the same limit holds: it lends type, density, palette, and one signature move, while navigation and controls stay the standard ones for the platform, web components on the web and native controls in an app.

Write each direction's first viewport as the product's shell first: the navigation, the work areas and what each is for, the data the visitor reads first and its states, and then where the signature move lives. Expression may never obscure the task, state, or familiar affordance. Name the signature move concretely, so the comp and the build can find it: service health drawn as a transit map, a schedule set in a timetable's column rhythm. A direction whose world shows up only as a colour scheme has not found its move yet. When you weigh fused challengers, product clarity includes reading as a working product of this category.

## Comps

The comp is the product screen, in the direction's committed palette: its shell and navigation with a distinct area for each job and, where there is data, filters over what they scope and charts and tables with clear states. The world enters only through type, palette, density, and the one signature move; it never supplies the page's organisation, so a working screen never reads as a newspaper, a poster, or any other artifact of the world. Every control is a standard one the visitor already knows how to use, a web component on the web and the platform's native control in an app: buttons, tabs, inputs, selects, filters, tables with sortable headers, navigation that reads as navigation. Never a costume of the world's own interface: a terminal's function-key bar or command prompt, an instrument's bezel, ruled ledger paper standing in for a table. A comp an engineer could not build from the platform's standard components is a picture of the tool, not the tool. The finish bar is the best product in the category: an aligned grid, consistent spacing, a real type scale, and clear hierarchy. The signature move adds to a screen that is already that clean; it never stands in for it.

Prompt with the screen's real content: the product name, realistic data with plausible values and units, real labels, and one state worth seeing (an alert, a degraded service, an empty filter result), never placeholder tiles. State colours (red for critical, amber for degraded) sit on top of the world's palette only where they carry meaning, and a headline number that moves over time shows its recent history, with the onset marked when something changed.

Comps two and three vary the product's organisation, never its world coverage: the navigation model (side rail, top bar, command-first), how the work areas divide the screen, which data leads, the density, and where the signature move sits. Each must be recognisably different from the first at thumbnail size; a variant only its prompt can tell apart adds no choice. A variant that adds world material, texture, or ornament goes further in the wrong direction; on a working screen, more world is a costume.

Self-check every render: with the name covered, does it read as a product of its category, could the visitor do the task from it, and is it at least as clean as the category standard and more distinctive than it? If it reads as an artifact of the world first, regenerate with the shell and the work areas named region by region and the world held to its four contributions.
# Operate mode depth (and Read notes)

When design SERVES the product: app UIs, admin dashboards, settings panels, data tables, tools, authenticated surfaces, anything where the user is in a task. The essentials live in SKILL.md's modes and [craft-floor.md](craft-floor.md); this file is extended depth, written for Operate surfaces. Read surfaces (docs, guides, long-form) take SKILL.md's Read mode plus this file's typography and consistency rules; their prose measure and navigation matter more than component density.

## The product slop test

Familiarity is often a feature here. The test is whether a category-fluent user can trust the interface immediately or must pause at every subtly-off component.

Product UI's failure mode isn't flatness, it's strangeness without purpose: over-decorated buttons, mismatched form controls, gratuitous motion, display fonts where labels should be, invented affordances for standard tasks. The bar is earned familiarity. The tool should disappear into the task.

## Typography

- **One family is often right.** Product UIs don't need display/body pairing. A well-tuned sans carries headings, buttons, labels, body, data.
- **Fixed rem scale, not fluid.** Clamp-sized headings don't serve product UI. Users view at consistent DPI, and a fluid h1 that shrinks in a sidebar looks worse, not better.
- **Tighter scale ratio.** 1.125–1.2 between steps is typical. More type elements here than on brand surfaces; exaggerated contrast creates noise.
- **Line length still applies for prose** (65–75ch). Data and compact UI can run denser; tables at 120ch+ are fine.

## Color

Product defaults to Restrained. A single surface can earn Committed (a dashboard where one category color carries a report, an onboarding flow with a drenched welcome screen), but Restrained is the floor.

- State-rich semantic vocabulary: hover, focus, active, disabled, selected, loading, error, warning, success, info. Standardize these.
- Accent color used for primary actions, current selection, and state indicators only, not decoration.
- A second neutral layer for sidebars, toolbars, and panels (slightly cooler or warmer than the content surface).

## Layout

- Responsive behavior is structural (collapse sidebar, responsive table, breakpoint-driven columns), not fluid typography.

## Components

Every interactive component has: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error. Don't ship with half of these.

- Skeleton states for loading, not spinners in the middle of content.
- Empty states that teach the interface, not "nothing here."
- Consistent affordances across the surface. Same button shape. Same form-control vocabulary. Same icon style.
- Overlays escape their container. An absolutely positioned dropdown inside an `overflow: hidden` or `overflow: auto` ancestor gets clipped; reach for `<dialog>`, the popover API, `position: fixed`, or a portal.

## Motion

- 150–250 ms on most transitions. Users are in flow; don't make them wait for choreography.
- Motion conveys state, not decoration. State change, feedback, loading, reveal: nothing else.
- No orchestrated page-load sequences. Product loads into a task; users don't want to watch it load.

## Product constraints

- Decorative motion that doesn't convey state.
- Inconsistent component vocabulary across screens. If the "save" button looks different in two places, one is wrong.
- Display fonts in UI labels, buttons, data.
- Reinventing standard affordances for flavor (custom scrollbars, weird form controls, non-standard modals).
- Heavy color or full-saturation accents on inactive states.
- Modal as first thought. Modals are usually laziness. Exhaust inline / progressive alternatives first.

## Product permissions

Product can afford things brand surfaces can't.

- System fonts and familiar sans defaults.
- Standard navigation patterns: top bar + side nav, breadcrumbs, tabs, command palettes.
- Density. Tables with many rows, panels with many labels, dense information when users need it.
- Consistency over surprise. The same visual vocabulary screen to screen is a virtue; delight is saved for moments, not pages.
# New visual work

Use this flow for a new surface or a replacement visual identity. PRODUCT.md owns product truth. DESIGN.md owns durable visual decisions. A surface brief keeps strategy that belongs to one route or artifact. Complete [init.md](init.md) first when PRODUCT.md is missing; a missing DESIGN.md does not route back to init.

For a chosen comp’s region map, see [region-map.md](region-map.md) for the command sequence and schema.

## 1. Decide what is already true

Read DESIGN.md, representative code, tokens, components, and assets.

- **Redesign:** preserve product truth, content, function, constraints, and explicit brand commitments; replace the old visual world rather than polishing it. The old look is evidence of what the subject is, not authority over what it becomes.
- **Established world:** inherit it. A missing DESIGN.md does not erase a coherent identity already in code; document that identity instead of inventing a replacement.
- **Incomplete brand:** preserve confirmed assets and recognizable traits, then expand the system with the user for this surface.
- **Seeded world:** DESIGN.md's frontmatter names a catalog `world:` (written by `impeccable world <id>`) and no code carries it yet; styles that predate the seed, such as a starter template's CSS, do not carry it. The person already chose this world, so it is the established world even when the boot reports no visual authority: never roll, re-pick, or invent a replacement on your own initiative, but an explicit request from the person for a redesign or a different world overrides this and is a redesign (step 4 of **Create or replace the visual world**, in [new-work-world.md](new-work-world.md
- **No visual authority:** create a new world with the user.

A section, component, feature, or state inside an established surface inherits that surface. Never turn a local addition into a new identity exercise.

## 2. Ask what will change the work

Before implementation, get the user's answer through the structured question tool when available. Ask two or three related questions; a precise request needs only a compact confirmation. Skip settled facts, not the confirmation: DESIGN.md settles the visual world, not this surface's purpose or concept.

- **Operate:** the task, information, important states, frequency, constraints.

Across modes, ask what success looks like, what must remain untouched, and what would make a polished result feel wrong. Never ask for CSS values or canned aesthetic lanes. Present them on the decision page as full cards of equal salience, the dealt lead under kicker THE ROLL, with steer and re-roll; the user locks one. Each card declares `kind`: `assigned` on the dealt lead, `dealt` on the other dealt structures, and `challenger` with its `catalogId` (the SOURCE ID) on a challenger that won its place. No canon card and no pick card at surface scope: the world is settled, so every card visualizes composition, not identi

### Create or replace the visual world

Read [new-work-world.md](new-work-world.md) now and follow it: this path's steps, the roll and the decision page live there. Come back for step 4 once a direction is locked.

The execution contract, comp-led or code-led, is never asked inside a round; the page's toggle handles the exception. An Operate or Read surface is code-led whatever the project records: working screens and documents come out better built than pictured. A Persuade or Experience surface takes the recorded default: read it from `.impeccable/config.json` (`buildPath`), the gitignored `.impeccable/config.local.json` winning where one machine differs from the team's committed value; with neither, comp-led is the default whenever image generation exists. concept-seed's PRESENTATION block prints the 

## 4. Commit the world

Pick a color strategy before picking colors: Restrained (neutrals tinted from the world plus one accent; common on screens people operate or read, where the mode's rules still ask colour to do real jobs), Committed (one saturated color carries 30-60% of the surface), Full palette (3-4 named roles), or Drenched (the surface IS the color). Persuade and Experience surfaces have permission for the bolder strategies; take them when the brief allows. Color commits at page scale: fields that own whole regions, not accents scattered over a neutral ground. Dark or light is never a default: write one se

Choose faces like objects from the subject's world, in the mode's register. Operate and Read surfaces are well served by system stacks and workhorse UI faces; Persuade and Experience surfaces want faces with a point of view, and these training-data defaults mean you stopped looking: Fraunces, Playfair Display, Cormorant, Lora, Crimson, Newsreader, Syne, Space Grotesk, Space Mono, IBM Plex, Inter-as-display, DM Sans, DM Serif, Outfit, Plus Jakarta Sans, Instrument Sans. Naming one of these faces anyway requires a reason no other face could satisfy, and a subject association is never that reason

Calibration: AI-generated interfaces cluster around a few looks regardless of subject: warm cream ground, high-contrast serif display, and a terracotta or signal-red accent; near-black with one neon accent and glowing edges; broadsheet-editorial hairlines, italic display serif, and small tracked mono labels; flat saturated ink with black boxes, hard offset shadows, and heavy condensed display type. All are legitimate when the brief calls for them. Where the brief leaves the aesthetic free, landing in one means the self-check failed: if someone could guess your aesthetic from the category alone

Your measured rendition prior: warm, bookish, family, and child-facing subjects come out as cream grounds, serif display with italic accents, and lamplight, even when the assigned direction never asked for them. Treat that first palette as already spent. Before writing code, reread your OWN-WORLD block: when it says cream, paper, parchment, ivory, or lamplight for a Persuade surface the brief did not pin, the rendition failed and you rework it from the world's saturated materials first. The same subject renders as bookcloth, thread, jacket, and endpaper color on other models; nothing about the

## 5. Record the decision

Before code, record the chosen direction as a development-only contract under `## Direction contract` in the relevant surface brief. A direction contract is durable route or artifact strategy, so create or update the brief even when no other surface strategy needs persistence. Use six short blocks, roughly 150 words; do not spend tool calls counting words. THESIS: the one idea this surface owns and the category-default arrangement it refuses. OWN-WORLD: the palette and component language, specific enough to be recognizable with all content removed. STORY: what the visitor understands, believes

On a new or replacement world, DESIGN.md is written at finish, from the built world, by the shipped documenter (section 7); a rulebook written before the build gets defended against reality instead of describing it, and hands the design-system detector an unstable target. A new world shipped with no DESIGN.md is still an incomplete run. An ordinary extension does not rewrite DESIGN.md.

After writing, read the brief once more and verify that all six contract blocks and the seed reference (or `seed: none (unavailable)` when the roll printed that, or `seed: none (pinned)` when a direction pinned whole skipped it) are present before building.

Keep the brief small: scope and visitor mode; audience, job, action/task, proof/content, and constraints; chosen direction and memorable moment; unresolved decisions. Do not copy global product truth or DESIGN.md tokens into it.

On a comp-led build, whenever any image generation is available (a harness-native tool or the API fallback `impeccable context` reports), the locked direction is visualized before it is built, never skipped: load [visualize.md](visualize.md) and follow it, three compositional options put before the user for approval, the chosen card's decision comp plus two variations. This step is proven to produce the most compositional and ambitious work. A comp locked in a surface-scope structure round has already discharged this round (Create a whole surface inside an established world, above). On a code-

For `shape`, return the selected direction to [shape.md](shape.md) and stop before persistence or implementation.

## 6. Build with full commitment

Build the assigned direction, not a safer interpretation of it. The form supplies structure, reading order, component conventions, and native motion; the product supplies every fact. Commit every atom: nav, buttons, inputs, and links are rebuilt in the form's vocabulary, and a stock component inside a committed form is a lapse. Land the first build fully committed; the passes that follow exist to make the committed thing clear and effective, never to dilute it. In unattended work, the safe rendition is the known risk.

### Comp-led: the comp is a measured contract

On a comp-led build, read [new-work-comp.md](new-work-comp.md) before writing the spec or any code, and follow it: the measured contract, the spec, and the build-phase gates live there.

### Both paths

- **The first viewport is a thesis, not a header.** Demonstrate the mechanism immediately, at the scale the form has in life; do not trap the concept inside a standard hero or card shell. The memory test: if someone left after one viewport, what would they describe an hour later? If the honest answer is a mood, the concept has not committed yet.
- **Prove, don't claim.** Show the subject doing its job: the interface at work, the mechanism dramatized, specifics a competitor could not copy-paste. Demonstration data is design material: author it at full fidelity and label it synthetic; claims stay uninventable.
- **Author the assets; never substitute chrome.** Great surfaces live on carefully made content: names, entries, copy, covers, thumbnails, textures. In greenfield work every blank the ask round left open is yours to author at production fidelity; content is authorable, claims are labelable, no section is omittable. Gradients, glass, generic icon tiles, and many-vertex `clip-path` polygons where an authored asset belongs are the gap wearing chrome; the detector flags the last two.
- **Draw a print material in its own technique.** On a code-led build, a world whose illustration is engraved, etched, or pen-and-ink is drawn as line: strokes carry the form, hatching (SVG patterns clipped to each shape) carries the tone, and colour sits inside the lines as a translucent wash. Flat fills under a thin outline read as clip-art, which the finish reviewer sends back for a rebuild. Use the world's own assets or one drawn subject per plate; never write a drawing engine.
- **Build the form's web leverage.** When the chosen world names a technique (canvas, WebGL, view transitions, generative motion), build the technique itself, not a static imitation of it.
- **Pace the scroll like a studio.** Vary density, scale, image, motion, and quiet inside one grammar; a dense passage earns a quiet one, and the page ends anchored by a real close. One spacing rhythm throughout, with more space above a heading than below it.
- **Use real, verified imagery when the brief implies it.** Search for the subject's physical object rather than the category; one decisive photo beats five mediocre ones. Verify stock URLs resolve.
- **Author motion as material.** Give the page the form's native motion once, orchestrated, rather than scattered hover effects. Bound expensive effects and keep content visible by default.

Preserve semantics, accessibility, performance, responsiveness, project conventions, and working behavior.

## 7. Inspect and finish

Inspect the surface's target sizes in one capture pass per breakpoint. On the web, `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable first-viewport <page> --thesis <FIRST VIEWPORT's selector> --action <primary action's selector> --capture .impeccable/review` is that pass: it writes `desktop.png` and `mobile.png` and checks the fold, gaps, sample labels (`--figures-supplied` for figures the user gave) and a dead action; build no screenshot harness of your own. On a native platform (`ios` / `android` / `adaptive`), the shipped device classes per OS, captured from the simulator or emulator the way th

A capture is evidence only when it is valid, and you validate before you send. Settle or disable entrance motion first: an element hidden by animation timing reads as a missing element and gets fixed into a regression. Capture full-page shots from the document top. Capture the comp comparison at the comp's own pixel dimensions. Then open every file once and confirm it shows what its name claims: no black or blank regions, no wrong section behind a right filename, no half-loaded state. A malformed capture sent onward costs the whole round; the reviewer answers it with `disposition: recapture` a

After that confirmation the build thread's polishing is over: no further defect hunts, micro-edit scripts, or rebuilds here (an open build-phase gate is not a defect hunt; it closes as above); whatever remains ships through the handoffs, where a fresh context does the finding better and cheaper. On the web, where this harness runs no design hook, run `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --json` on the changed targets once here, fix what is mechanical, and pass the remaining findings to the reviewer; a hookless web build that skips this ships every tell the hook exists to catch.

Then spawn the shipped finish reviewer, `impeccable-finish-reviewer` (`impeccable_finish_reviewer` in codex; `/impeccable-finish-reviewer` in Cursor; on GitHub Copilot say "Use the impeccable-finish-reviewer agent"), with the original request, confirmed answers, the artifact path, the screenshot paths, the direction contract, existing hook findings, the QUALITY BAR card and approved comp paths (a code-led build has no approved comp; the chosen decision comp rides in that slot as the critique reference, named as such), on a comp-led build the build state (`.impeccable/build/state.json`), the sp

Act on the disposition word; there are exactly four. **recapture**: the evidence failed, not the build. Recapture what the return names under the capture-validity rules, then run a full review over the new evidence. A review conducted on invalid evidence binds nothing, and a verdict pass may never follow it. **rebuild**: fidelity failed wholesale, not in patches. Skip the fix batch and execute the rebuild immediately: re-derive the named regions, produce the named assets, and send the result back for a fresh full review, never a verdict pass; a rebuild replaces regions wholesale, so the whole 

A rebuild and a fix round share one asset rule: a raster either round creates or replaces is still asset work under [visualize.md](visualize.md)'s Produce section and keeps its **provenance** like every build raster, and a raster the round abandons is deleted in the same batch. On a comp-led build, record the final review disposition with `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable build-phase finish --disposition <ship|fix|rebuild|recapture>` before the final response. Never record `fix` to end a run over an open gate: take the route th

The final response opens with the result, not the process: when the build finished, one line saying the page is ready and exactly how to open it (the running dev server's URL, else the command that serves it, else the file path), then the verdict at its scope; when it did not, that line says what is left and still how to open what exists. # Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

<!-- Source of the answers: the coordinator's brief for issue #20 (2026-11-23), plus AGENTS.md, docs/design/design.md
and the take-home brief. No interactive interview took place; nothing below is invented beyond those sources. -->

## Platform

web

## Users
- **Travellers** (primary): ordinary passengers of the airline Ocean Above who want to book a flight by typing what they
  want ("I want to fly from Guangzhou to Lima"), check the route and price, and later look up their tickets. They use
  a desktop browser or, just as often, a phone.
- **Take-home reviewers**: engineers evaluating the demo (`ocean-above.potafree.net`, or `docker compose up` locally).
  They read the design doc, try edge cases (unserved cities, ambiguous names, refusing to confirm) and check that every
  number on screen is right and that nothing is booked without an explicit confirmation.

## Product Purpose
A natural-language flight booking assistant for Ocean Above. Core jobs:
1. Ask for a flight in plain language and get a quote: the cheapest route with every leg, every transfer city, the
   total distance and the price.
2. Check that full route, distance and price, then book by clicking an explicit confirm control.
3. Look up booked tickets (in chat or on My tickets).
4. Re-read any past conversation (History).
Success: the user can verify every fact before paying, and a reviewer finds no number that does not come from the
backend's deterministic computation.

## Positioning
The language model only understands and phrases; routes, distances, prices, nearest served cities and bookings are
computed by deterministic backend code from `locations.db`. Every number shown comes from a tool result, and booking
happens only when the user clicks a one-time confirm card. The interface makes that split visible: facts live in
structured cards, not in chat prose.

## Operating Context
- Chat screen: conversation list (drawer on phones), messages with streamed assistant text, and cards: quote,
  booking request (confirm), ticket, ticket list, no-service (nearest served cities), ambiguous city (candidates with
  distinguishing facts), unknown city, notice.
- My tickets and History (read-only conversations) pages; a simple login (fixed dev account; Google later).
- Quotes expire; a booking can be refused as stale / expired / busy / data unavailable and the UI must say what to do.

## Capabilities and Constraints
- Numbers are shown only from the backend's `*_display` fields; the frontend never formats or recomputes numbers.
- Quote and confirm cards must make the legs, transfer cities, total distance and price prominent (take-home req. 7).
- Unserved city → tell the user and show the nearest served city (req. 8).
- Nothing is booked without the user clicking confirm on that exact quote; the LLM cannot book.
- Mobile is first-class: ≥ 360 px wide, touch targets ≥ 44×44, no horizontal scroll.
- Stack: Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS; shadcn/ui-style components copied into the repo. Minimal dependencies.
- English UI copy.

## Brand Commitments
- Name: **Ocean Above** (fictional airline from the take-home). No logo or brand assets exist.
- Character (DESIGN.md §1): calm, trustworthy, precise; no decorative gradients or illustrations; prices and distances
  always also appear in a structured card; colour never means two things.

## Evidence on Hand
- `locations.db` (cities, hubs, links) and the contract fixtures in `contract/fixtures/` (realistic quotes, tickets,
  conversations). No testimonials, customers or marketing claims exist and none may be invented.

## Product Principles
1. Facts before prose: anything the user must verify is in a structured card.
2. Confirmation is explicit and unmistakable; its state (awaiting, booked, expired, out of date) is always legible.
3. Every failure says what happened and what to do next.
4. Phone and desktop are equals.

## Accessibility & Inclusion
WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text and icons; keyboard reachable; visible focus; status never by colour
alone; reduced motion respected.

MODE RULES (operate, from /Volumes/ZT/repos/llc2026/ocean-above-it04-design/.claude/skills/impeccable/reference/mode-operate.md). They govern this surface's directions and every comp you write or judge for it, the decision comps included; where shared guidance conflicts, these win.
DIRECTIONS
Someone who uses tools like this one should know where everything is before they notice the world. The world lends four things and only these: type, palette, density, and one signature move. It never supplies the layout, the navigation model, or the controls. Colour is part of the world's contribution, and it does real jobs: a committed palette for the shell (a coloured rail or header, a tinted ground), state colours, data series, selection, and the signature move. A grey screen with one accent colour is the category default without the category's polish, not restraint.

Read every candidate, the assigned direction, and every challenger through that limit before you fuse or judge it. A world taken from a tool or instrument the audience operates (a terminal, a scope, a control panel, a cockpit) or from a fictional interface comes back as a costume of that tool on a working screen: take from it only what transfers as type, palette, density, and a signature move, or replace it from your list. When a catalog world's source is itself an interface language, the same limit holds: it lends type, density, palette, and one signature move, while navigation and controls stay the standard ones for the platform, web components on the web and native controls in an app.

Write each direction's first viewport as the product's shell first: the navigation, the work areas and what each is for, the data the visitor reads first and its states, and then where the signature move lives. Expression may never obscure the task, state, or familiar affordance. Name the signature move concretely, so the comp and the build can find it: service health drawn as a transit map, a schedule set in a timetable's column rhythm. A direction whose world shows up only as a colour scheme has not found its move yet. When you weigh fused challengers, product clarity includes reading as a working product of this category.
COMPS
The comp is the product screen, in the direction's committed palette: its shell and navigation with a distinct area for each job and, where there is data, filters over what they scope and charts and tables with clear states. The world enters only through type, palette, density, and the one signature move; it never supplies the page's organisation, so a working screen never reads as a newspaper, a poster, or any other artifact of the world. Every control is a standard one the visitor already knows how to use, a web component on the web and the platform's native control in an app: buttons, tabs, inputs, selects, filters, tables with sortable headers, navigation that reads as navigation. Never a costume of the world's own interface: a terminal's function-key bar or command prompt, an instrument's bezel, ruled ledger paper standing in for a table. A comp an engineer could not build from the platform's standard components is a picture of the tool, not the tool. The finish bar is the best product in the category: an aligned grid, consistent spacing, a real type scale, and clear hierarchy. The signature move adds to a screen that is already that clean; it never stands in for it.

Prompt with the screen's real content: the product name, realistic data with plausible values and units, real labels, and one state worth seeing (an alert, a degraded service, an empty filter result), never placeholder tiles. State colours (red for critical, amber for degraded) sit on top of the world's palette only where they carry meaning, and a headline number that moves over time shows its recent history, with the onset marked when something changed.

Comps two and three vary the product's organisation, never its world coverage: the navigation model (side rail, top bar, command-first), how the work areas divide the screen, which data leads, the density, and where the signature move sits. Each must be recognisably different from the first at thumbnail size; a variant only its prompt can tell apart adds no choice. A variant that adds world material, texture, or ornament goes further in the wrong direction; on a working screen, more world is a costume.

Self-check every render: with the name covered, does it read as a product of its category, could the visitor do the task from it, and is it at least as clean as the category standard and more distinctive than it? If it reads as an artifact of the world first, regenerate with the shell and the work areas named region by region and the world held to its four contributions.
